data.name: Lonvera

audit.sub: Second opinion, from the account's own numbers, 12 months to August 2026. Findings only.

wins.title: The flow layer, back to its own pre-rebuild rate
wins.detail: Clean flow revenue runs $70,322 a month against $93,283 before the rebuild. The single biggest piece is replenishment, which earned $201k in the year and has been off since May with seven drafts and nothing live.

wins.title: Campaign targeting, aimed at people who buy
wins.detail: Segmented sends earn $0.342 to $0.422 aimed at buyers and engaged audiences and $0.028 to $0.031 aimed at prospects. Three non-buyer sends in August reached about 90,000 people between them for roughly $2,600.

wins.title: Re-entry windows, and one unsuppressed checkout flow
wins.detail: 21 days on site and browse, 14 on checkout, against 4 to 7. CKC Checkout Abandonment carries no cross-flow suppression and is the largest of the three at 37,752 delivered.

wins.title: Flow volume
wins.detail: Outside one flow the rebuilt set hardly sends: 396 and 462 emails in a year on the two browse flows, 411 and 141 on added-to-cart, 125 on welcome.

wins.title: Nothing has been tested
wins.detail: No live flow has a second variant and no campaign of 213 carries a test. Every figure in this document is a single guess that was never checked.

wins.title: The traffic the funnel does not convert
wins.detail: Opt-in is bypassed deliberately, so the open question is where a visitor who does not buy ends up, and whether anything can reach them.

audit.title: Lonvera: a read of the Klaviyo account

findings.body:
For eighteen months email tracked the business. The store grew from $164k a month to about $1.5M and email's share held: 24.0%, 23.4%, 21.3% across three half-years. Since March it has run at 11.9%.

At the account's own 22.2%, the last six months would have earned $2.23M instead of $1.19M.

Worth saying: the store did not stop growing, it is up 20% half on half. The business did not lose that money. The owned channel stopped taking its share of it, and whether those flows were creating demand or harvesting it is a holdout question, not an opinion.

chart.metricLabel: Email and SMS as a share of store

findings.title: Email held 22% of a growing store for 18 months, then halved

findings.body:
Of the first 2,500 profiles created in August, 65 consented through a form and 1,123 arrived through the API carrying order properties. Paid social goes straight into a Checkout Champ funnel, so people arrive as buyers, not subscribers. That is a choice, and it is why the welcome flow sits around seventeenth by revenue.

The open question is the traffic it does not convert. Someone who lands, does not buy and leaves: what list do they join, and can they trigger anything? Worth measuring before anyone argues for a popup.
findings.title: Opt-in is bypassed by design

findings.body: 3,288 in March, 929 in June, 617 in August, while total opt-ins rose from 5,292 to 9,877. The list is fed by purchase, not capture. Noting it so it is not mistaken for a fault.
findings.title: Form submissions down 81%, consistent with the funnel

findings.body: Eight forms, three live. Two built on 11 March and untouched since, one from November 2023, five drafts behind them including an A/B clone that never shipped. Low priority given the funnel, but it is the cheapest thing here to test.
findings.title: The three live popups have never been iterated

findings.body:
85,293 new subscribers against 36,839 unsubscribes. Since April the intake runs three to five times the earlier rate.

Unsubscribes moved with it: 0.270% of delivered in November, 0.656% in May, 0.432% in August. Spam went 0.013% to 0.036%, still inside Klaviyo's 0.05% line. Both charts below cover the same months.
findings.title: The list is growing fast and deliverability is paying for it

findings.body:
Sign-ups fell every month from 1,594 last September to 191 in August. 44 campaigns delivered 470,629 messages for $9,261, and thirteen of them returned nothing. Unsubscribes run 0.555% against email's 0.324%.

On these numbers the channel costs more list health than it returns.
findings.title: SMS: 88% fewer opt-ins, $9,261 of revenue

findings.body:
Through February campaigns earned $0.271 a delivered email; since March, $0.148. Two things to know before reading anything into that.

From 9 June every send excludes active subscribers, subscriber cohorts and recent buyers. No send before that date did. So the earlier figure carries recurring Skio revenue that was going to land anyway and the later one does not. Not the same measurement.

And the drop came first. April and May were the worst months of the year, $0.100 and $0.113, with no exclusions and only 5 and 8 sends. After the exclusions started the rate rose to $0.185 in July.

What is solid: the segmented sends work aimed at buyers ($0.422) and engaged audiences ($0.342 to $0.375), and fail aimed at prospects. Three Vital Belle non-buyer sends in August, about 30,000 each, returned $0.031, $0.028 and $0.028.
findings.title: Revenue per email halved, and the audience rules changed underneath it

findings.body:
Ranked by revenue per delivered email, the winners are curiosity-led and education-first, not promotional, and they beat the $0.214 average by three to four times.

That is the most useful thing in the account: the audience responds to the science and the story. These concepts run once as a campaign and then stop.

findings.title: The best concepts earn three to four times the average

findings.body:
Twelve campaigns in February, none in March, five in April, then 21, 29 and 24 through June to August. No SMS in March, April or June either.

A month of silence costs about a month of campaign revenue, and the swing from nothing to double the old cadence is harder on a list than either level.
findings.title: March 2026: not a single campaign went out

findings.body:
Stripping what the flows did not really earn, billing reminders and order confirmations that ride a committed charge, and setting the welcome flows aside as a deliberate choice: clean flow revenue averaged $93,283 a month before the rebuild and $70,322 over the last four. A gap of about $23,000 a month, $276,000 a year.

What was retired, and when it last sent: Customer Thank You ($387,924, until July), Welcome Series ($203,803, until March), Replenishment ($200,771, until May), Site Abandonment ($53,943 and $37,549, until April), Welcome with reminder ($51,593, until March), Abandoned Checkout ($33,544, until March).

What replaced them, and when it started: the MP set came on between June and July. CKC Checkout Abandonment ($87,736 from June) is the only one earning at scale. Checkout Shopify ($8,653), Order Confirmation ($8,418), Site Abandonment Upstack ($7,705), Checkout Upstack ($5,011), Site Abandonment ($4,020), all from June or July.

So the old set was switched off between March and July and the new set came on in June and July. Whether that overlap was planned, and why, is the one thing the account cannot show.
findings.title: Flow revenue is running $23k a month below where it was

findings.body:
A second tracking layer copies every Shopify event, so there is a parallel flow for each. Most do suppress their twin properly. One does not: CKC Checkout Abandonment has no cross-flow suppression and is the largest at 37,752 delivered.

The bigger number is volume. Outside that flow the rebuilt set hardly sends: 396 and 462 emails in a year on the two browse flows, 411 and 141 on added-to-cart, 125 on welcome.
findings.title: The rebuilt flows barely fire

findings.body:
Seven flows with replenishment in the name, none live. The one that ran earned $201k in the year to August and stopped paying out in May. On a 30-day supply that is the flow that should never be off.

Cart abandonment does run, twice. Absent entirely: back in stock, bounce back after a first order, VIP, and an evergreen best-of.

chart.note: 117 flows exist, 25 are live. The 87 drafts are not all junk: three of them earned $792k between them last year before being switched off.

findings.title: Seven replenishment flows, none of them running

findings.body:
Site and browse wait 21 days before someone can re-enter, checkout waits 14. We run 4 to 7.

On a considered purchase, three visits in a fortnight is the strongest signal available and the second and third currently get nothing. The same flows are each missing four prescribed filters, which is what lets a flow keep mailing someone who has already bought.
findings.title: Re-entry is set to 21 days

findings.body:
No live flow contains a message with a second variant. No campaign of 213 carries a test. One popup has A/B switched on and it is a draft that never shipped.

Every number above is a single guess that was never checked against an alternative.
